claim:fixed-boundary.proposition: OBSERVED (partial pass): against an immovable wall mean barrier_velocity = 0 (within ±1e-3) while contact force accumulates. Quantitative match to the Peskin ratchet rate still pending a digitized reference.

claim:rigid-movable-boundary.proposition: OBSERVED: a drag-loaded movable wall settles to a non-zero velocity. Whether the stall force stays within the Peskin-1993 bound is NOT yet checked.

claim:actin-to-membrane-force-handshake.proposition: OBSERVED (option B, magnitude-conserving): the coupler now sizes the osmotic offset so its integrated membrane force equals the actin contact force; force_residual ≈ 0 every step. CAVEAT: pressure-mediated effective-force handshake, not an independent per-vertex check (that is option A, blocked by a pymem3dg applied-force segfault — tracked).

claim:membrane-to-actin-displacement-fee.proposition: TARGET (not yet tested): per-step mesh-position feedback preserves mesh quality and keeps tips inside their box potentials. Mesh-quality is currently inferred, not measured.

claim:flexible-mem3dg-boundary.proposition: OBSERVED: under actin pressure the vesicle inflates. That load is redistributed across filaments / relaxed off the rigid curve is NOT yet quantified — inflation alone is not ratchet success.

claim:coupled-ratchet-cycle-fv-reproduct.proposition: TARGET (not yet tested): the closed loop reproduces the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition. No benchmark comparison has been run.

narrative.question:
Can a particle-based actin Brownian ratchet (ReaDDy) push against a deformable membrane
(Mem3DG) through a physically faithful bidirectional coupler, and does increasing boundary
realism — fixed wall → rigid movable object → flexible membrane — reproduce the
force/velocity signatures that distinguish a flexible-membrane ratchet (Inoue 2015) from
the classical rigid-wall regime (Peskin 1993)?

decisions.title: Which numerical tolerances define "matches Peskin / Inoue"?
decisions.detail:
The rigid-wall and stall-force tests need agreed quantitative bounds before their
stub predicates can become evaluated pass/fail criteria.

decisions.title: Spherical mesh-vertex feedback or planar wall_radius for the canonical F-V run?
decisions.detail:
membrane-to-actin-displacement-feedback supports both boundary-update modes; the choice
fixes how the closed-loop reproduction study advances the barrier.

decisions.title: Where do the Peskin (1993) and Inoue (2015) reference curves come from for the overlays?
decisions.detail:
Benchmark figures require digitized/analytic reference data. Decide whether to digitize the
published figures, recompute the closed-form Peskin curve, or both, and register them as
investigation inputs.
